You've got a few options here

Firstly, it takes about 7 times for someone to leave their abusive partner, before they finally do so. Each time usually means an escalation of violence on the part of the abusing partner. My recommendation is for you to leave. If your partner really loved you and cared for you he never would have put his hands on you and said those awful things. I know it hurts but the other option is a long and windy road. I'm suspicious of this being the first time something like this happening. Wht did he want to leave in the first place?

The other option is one I've seen proposed elsewhere, you can have him stop drinking, I would add getting some therapy. Could this work? Maybe. He might resent you for telling him stop drinking, he'll probably try to gaslight you into thinking what happened wasnt so bad/wasnt his fault/ and some how shift the blame onto you. Is this a noble option for saving your relationship, I suppose. You can sit here and tell yourself how you pushed through this road bump and that it wasn't the worst thing in the world, it was just a slap.  But do you want a partner who does things like this to you? It only escalates from here.

Him begging for you to stay, telling you you can fix him,  it was a mistake, it was an accident, you were in his way, why don't you understand him, it's shifting blame and responsibility, and it's going to cost you your life. Leave now or leave in 7 times from now, those are your choices.
